title: ER leakage: the recombination fraction required and the 124Xe/125I double-vacancy hypothesis
question: If the event were a 64-71 keV electron recoil, what recombination fraction and fluctuation are required, how many 124Xe/125I/activation candidates existed, and is an unmodelled ER tail compatible with the empty region between the event and the ER band?
headline_result: An ER origin needs r = 0.939 vs beta mean 0.720 (958 of 1226 electrons missing, 6.4 sigma on the band-calibrated width); with the f = 0.20 charge suppression that reproduces LZ's 21 124Xe ROI events, 564 KK and <=1e4 125I decays leak <=1e-2 event-like events (flat extrapolation of LZ's own Fig.5 tail: 2.8e-3), and any tail giving O(1) event predicts 1-9 events in the empty gap (0 observed); ER leakage disfavoured at <~0.3%.
key_numbers: Nq=5179+-90; E_ee=69.6 keV (W=13.44); r_req=0.939 (0.938-0.945); sigma_Ne cal=150 e (k=0.50), raw 300 e excluded; LZ 6.7sigma = 6.8 half-widths = 8.7 Gaussian sigma; 124Xe 779 decays (564 KK); N_ROI(f=0/0.2/0.3)=15.6/21.3/67.6 vs 21.0+-6.3; N_V(KK,f=0.2)=2e-7..8e-4; N_V(125I,1e4 decays,f=0.2)<=0.02; continuum <=3e-3; LZ plateau extrapolation 2.8e-3 vs floor 1.6e-4; N_G=1-9 when N_V>=0.1; 125I rate at +8 d = 40% of peak
model_or_mechanism: NEST-LZ ER yields (Table S3) + Table S4 sigma_p fluctuation model calibrated to digitised Fig.4 bands; constant-Nq line loci with charge suppression f; four tail shapes; Poisson likelihood of 1-in-V/0-in-G; Bateman 125Xe->125I with 3.6 d effective removal
stance: neutral (constraint: disfavours the ER-leakage background at <~0.3%; does not discriminate NR from MSSI or neutrons)
